description: This line plot displays the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods—Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME—on Llama2 as a function of the co-occurrence number. The x-axis is labeled 'Co-occurrence Number' and uses a logarithmic scale, spanning from 10^1 to 10^3. The y-axis is labeled 'ACC (%)' and uses a linear scale, ranging from 60% to 80%. The 'Base' method is represented by a black line with solid circles; 'FT' is a blue line with triangle markers; 'IKE' is a red line with triangle markers; 'MEND' is a brown line with diamond markers; 'MEMIT' is a purple line with diamond markers; and 'ROME' is a green line with square markers. The 'ROME' line starts at approximately 72% ACC at 10^1 and rises steadily to about 78% ACC at 10^3. The 'MEND' line begins at about 66% ACC at 10^1 and increases to approximately 74% ACC at 10^3. The 'MEMIT' line starts at about 66% ACC at 10^1 and ends at approximately 72% ACC at 10^3. The 'FT' line begins at around 63% ACC at 10^1 and rises to about 68% ACC at 10^3. The 'IKE' line starts at approximately 65% ACC at 10^1 and stabilizes near 70% ACC across the entire range. The 'Base' line begins at 61% ACC at 10^1 and increases slightly to about 66% ACC at 10^3.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC) performance of six methods (Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME) on Llama2 across varying co-occurrence numbers. The x-axis represents 'Co-occurrence Number' on a logarithmic scale, ranging from 10^1 to 10^3, while the y-axis shows 'ACC (%)' on a linear scale from 60% to 80%. ROME consistently outperforms all other methods, achieving an accuracy of approximately 85% at the highest co-occurrence number. MEMIT and MEND exhibit similar trends, with MEMIT slightly surpassing MEND at lower co-occurrence numbers but falling behind at higher values. FT demonstrates the steepest growth rate, increasing by nearly 10% across the range, while Base remains relatively stable, showing minimal improvement. IKE starts with the highest initial accuracy but stabilizes at around 70%, falling behind MEMIT and MEND at higher co-occurrence numbers.
